title: POC weekly - batching & concurrency sprint review
summary: Weekly sync to review pilot throughput numbers after continuous-batching + concurrency tweaks. We compared baseline runs to the last 48h of traffic with prefix caching enabled. Main wins were improved tokens/sec and lower tail latency at target concurrency of 18; observed cost uplift at higher concurrency due to padding. Agreed next steps: Maya to share tuned config + cost breakdown, Jonah to run 1-hr stress run at 30 concurrent reqs, customer to validate tail latency on their staging traffic.
next_steps: Maya to share batching+concurrency config + perf graphs (by 2026-04-16)
Jonah to run 1-hour stress run at 30 concurrent requests and upload logs (by 2026-04-17)
VantageRX to validate 95th and 99th tail latency on staging using their replay (by 2026-04-20)
Schedule vendor security doc walkthrough if staging passes (owner: Ruchi)
action_items: Maya Patel | Share tuned batching config + cost breakdown + sample curl commands | 2026-04-16
Jonah Reed | Run 1-hour stress run at concurrency 30, collect per-token latency traces and KV hit rates | 2026-04-17
Priya Kumar | Run staging replay for 95th/99th latency validation and report anomalies | 2026-04-20

transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-04-14 15:00 UTC | Duration: 45 minutes | Attendees: Maya, Jonah (Redwood); Ruchi, Tom, Priya (VantageRX)

Summary section (auto): quick numbers review, config diff, plan for stress-run and validation.

[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): Okay, hey everyone, thanks for making time. Quick roll call, and then we'll jump into the numbers from the last 48 hours after the continuous-batching change.
[00:12] Ruchi (VantageRX CTO): Hi, yeah thanks. We had Priya and Tom here as well.
[00:16] Tom (SRE): Hey all.
[00:18] Priya: Hello.
[00:20] Jonah (Redwood SE): Hey team. I'm Jonah, I pushed the batching tweak late last night and watched the first wave this morning.
[00:27] Maya: Cool. Real quick agenda: one, present throughput and latency deltas; two, validate where we set concurrency targets; three, discuss queueing and backpressure behavior we observed; four, confirm next steps. Sound good?
[00:38] Ruchi: Yep.

--- Results review ---
[00:45] Jonah: Alright, so baseline - the customer baseline from last week, cold config, was averaging about 420 tokens per second per GPU cluster, tail 95th at ~420ms and 99th around 1.1s with concurrency=10. After enabling continuous batching and prefix KV cache we saw average tokens/sec jump to about 720 tokens/sec. That's with a concurrency target of 18 in the test harness.
[01:12] Priya: Quick clarification, when you say prefix KV cache, that's the prefix key-value caching right? Did you enable TTL or was it infinite?
[01:20] Jonah: Yeah, it's prefix K-V with a 6 hour TTL in this run. We also enabled cached key coalescing — that reduces repeated KV loads across requests with similar prefixes.
[01:31] Tom: The numbers look good on average, but can you show the distribution? Our primary concern is the 99th because the app is latency-sensitive for interactive mode.
[01:40] Jonah: Sure. The 95th dropped to ~250ms, 99th to ~720ms at concurrency 18. But we saw a small bump in token cost per request when we moved concurrency above 22 — mostly due to padding and larger batching windows.
[01:56] Maya: Right, and that's the classic latency vs cost tradeoff. We wanted to optimize for throughput without regressing tail latency beyond your SLO. Ruchi, remind me — your SLO was 95th under 300ms for interactive?
[02:07] Ruchi: Yes, 95th < 300ms ideally, 99th under 800ms acceptable.

--- Observations & weirdness ---
[02:15] Jonah: A few things we noticed. One: at high concurrency peaks (30+), queueing builds up in the request router and we start to see longer scheduling jitter — requests wait in the batching window longer and that pushes the 99th up. Two: when the model context length increases beyond 1k tokens for some of your longer prompts, batching efficiency decreases because of padding alignment.
[02:40] Priya: Padding alignment — is that per-token padding due to different sequences or because of KV cache misses?
[02:46] Jonah: Mostly sequence-length variance. KV cache helps when prefixes match; when they don't, you lose the prefix win and the batch contains a wider variety of lengths so mean tokens/sec drops and tail increases.
[02:56] Tom: We also noticed some intermittent spikes that correlated with our VPC NAT throughput saturation — when egress caps hit, we saw request queuing and timeouts. So part of the tail is infra not just the model.
[03:08] Maya: Good callout. So action for Tom to validate NAT throughput numbers and maybe bump out the egress for the pilot if needed.
[03:15] Tom: Yup, will do.

--- Tuning decisions ---
[03:20] Maya: So proposed tuning: keep concurrency target at 18 for interactive, hard cap at 24 so we don't see large padding-induced cost increases; enable prefix TTL 6 hours for staging; use dynamic batching windows that shrink when queue depth small to keep tail down; and set a focused canary for the high-concurrency stress run.
[03:39] Ruchi: I like the hard cap idea. Can we get a recommended config from you that we can drop into our envoy/router?
[03:45] Jonah: Yep. I'll share a YAML with target_concurrency:18, max_concurrency:24, batching_window_ms: default 8ms but dynamic down to 3ms under low queue, and batch_size_soft_limit tuned to prefer throughput but drop padding if mean seq length > 700.
[04:02] Priya: Real quick — you said dynamic down to 3ms, does that increase the number of small batches and hurt overall throughput?
[04:08] Jonah: Slightly on average, but it keeps the 95/99 tight. For interactive flows it's worth it. For bulk async inference we can flip a different profile.

--- Benchmark artifacts & links ---
[04:18] Maya: I uploaded the summary spreadsheet and the perf graphs to the shared drive: https://redwood.share/drive/vx-pilot/apr14. The run IDs are in the spreadsheet.
[04:27] Ruchi: Got it. I'll pull that after the call. Are you also going to share the raw traces?
[04:31] Jonah: Yes I'll upload per-token trace gists and the KV hit rate CSV. Note: traces have some redactions for IPs — automated transcribe sometimes swaps 'VPC' with 'vee-pee-see' in the logs.
[04:44] Tom: ha, yeah we've seen that.

--- Cost discussion ---
[04:48] Maya: On cost side, continuous batching gave about 32% better cost per 1k tokens at concurrency 18 vs baseline, but at concurrency >24 the per-token padded compute caused cost per 1k to increase ~10% over baseline. So there's a knee there.
[05:03] Priya: So if we run at steady 18 then we're in the sweet spot?
[05:06] Maya: Based on current traffic patterns yes. But if you have frequent peaks we recommend a burst policy: short-duration reserved burst to handle spikes or route spikes to a lower-cost fallback model for degraded quality.
[05:19] Ruchi: Fallback model — do you mean smaller mixed-quant model? We need to understand quality drop.
[05:23] Jonah: Exactly, a lower-precision quant model or smaller LLM variant; Redwood supports routing rules so you can fallback to a cheaper variant automatically when the queue depth gets high. We'll include a quality delta estimate from our eval harness.

--- Customer questions and edge cases ---
[05:36] Priya: If we enable longer TTL on prefix cache, what's the memory footprint? We have a node memory constraint.
[05:43] Jonah: Memory grows linearly with unique prefixes; based on your 24h traffic sample, 6-hour TTL would use ~22GB across the pool. We can trade off by sharding prefix keys and evicting low-hit keys more aggressively.
[05:55] Tom: Also wondering about cold start behavior after rolling deploys. We saw an increase in 99th for about 7 minutes post-deploy. Is that expected?
[06:02] Jonah: Some cold cache effect yes; our runtime warms KV on first requests, and continuous-batching benefits accrue after warm-up. For deploys we recommend staged rollouts (canary) and pre-warm routines where possible.

--- Agreement & next steps recap ---
[06:18] Maya: Quick recap: keep interactive concurrency target 18, cap 24; Jonah to run a stress test at 30 for an hour with the same traffic replay and share traces; Maya to share configs and cost breakdown; Tom to validate VPC NAT throughput; Priya to run staging replay and validate tail latency; meet again 2026-04-21.
[06:36] Ruchi: Sounds good. If staging shows failures we'll pull the burst reserve and trigger fallback to smaller model for spikes.

--- Closing ---
[06:44] Maya: Anything else?
[06:46] Priya: One ask — can you include a short snippet we can drop into our ingress to enforce the hard cap?
[06:51] Jonah: Yep we'll include the envoy/nginx snippet in the config bundle.
[06:54] Maya: Great. Thanks everyone. We'll follow up on action items and post artifacts.
[06:58] Tom: Thanks.
[07:00] Ruchi: Thanks, bye.

Notes: occasional transcription noise: 'K-V' spelled variously; 'VPC' sometimes 'V-P-C' in auto transcripts. Links referenced: perf spreadsheet, per-token traces, config gist.
